documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: the VIN decodes cleanly to an XR2 convertible, and a clean-title claim plus a Carfax snapshot (3 records) are given. The one disclosed defect is the faded paint on the hardtop. Floors, footwells, underside, soft-top fabric and running condition are not examined here.

price_value.rationale: No fair value or comps are supplied. The current bid of $5,500 and an expected hammer in the high four figures are reasonable for a low-mile, hardtop-equipped XR2 manual, and well inside the budget band. The value hinges on the floor and timing-belt unknowns, plus a likely $1.5-3k first-year catch-up.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, top-down car with a point of view, at a fraction of the budget. However, it is not one of the named bridge targets, parts for the chassis and trim are scarce, a 35-year-old turbo car's reliability is unproven, and resale is a thin enthusiast market.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Wylie, TX and the no-reserve auction closes in about 18 hours, so arranging a PPI before money moves is tight and not offered. The dealer is responsive and BaT shipping is available. CA smog readiness is unconfirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits are present: the turbo XR2 with a 5-speed, the original removable hardtop, a claimed 50k miles, one-family history, and complete original-looking trim and wheels. These are offset by the faded hardtop and an added trailer hitch.

ppi_focus: Floor pans, seat mounts, lower A-pillar to sill junction and spare well for rust; carpet padding for dampness or mildew
Soft top raised: fabric, rear window, latches and weatherstrip; water test if possible
Turbo shaft play, oil in the intercooler piping, and boost reading on the gauge under load
Crank pulley wobble and keyway condition; timing-belt condition and date
Compression test on all four cylinders, plus a cooling-system pressure test
Clutch engagement height and slip in 3rd and 4th under boost; master and slave cylinders for weeping; synchro grind on fast 2-3 shifts
Hitch mounting points and the rear crossmember/rails for towing stress
Fuel tank installation quality, lines and filler for leaks after the August 2026 replacement
SRS lamp, pop-up headlight motors, power windows, and gauges (oil pressure, boost, temperature)
Strut condition, mounts and CV boots, since original parts are scarce
what_would_change_verdict: Up: lifted-carpet and underside photos showing dry, rust-free floors and seat mounts.
Up: a dated timing-belt or water-pump receipt, plus a clean cold-start video with no smoke and a steady pulley.
Up: confirmation that an inspector can see the car before the close, with clean compression results.
Down: rust in the floors or sills, a damp interior, or an SRS or warning lamp that stays on.
Down: bidding pushes well past the high four figures with the floors and belt still unverified.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, open-top turbo runabout like this has a genuine point of view and costs far less than the budget band. However, it is not one of Jason's named bridge targets, and its parts scarcity, 35-year age and thin resale market work against the reliable, easy-to-resell bridge brief.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decodes to a 1991 Mercury Capri XR2 convertible, consistent with the listing's turbo 1.6, five-speed manual and 50k miles. The title is a claimed clean Indiana title, with a Carfax snapshot showing no reported accidents and 3 records. The photos establish straight bodywork, intact Capri-specific trim and spoilers, factory wheels, a clean cloth interior, a manual gear lever, and an engine bay that appears stock. The observed issues are the disclosed faded hardtop paint, an added trailer hitch, and a dealer-stated fuel tank and sender replacement in August 2026, for which no invoice or cause is given. None of the model-critical evidence is present: no floor or footwell photos were examined here, there is no timing-belt receipt, no cold-start video, no compression data, and no smog readiness. Warning-lamp status, tire age, soft-top fabric condition and completion of the 92V080000 airbag recall are also unknown. The auction is no reserve, closes in about 18 hours in Texas, and has no stated PPI access, so most of these questions must be answered by the dealer or a quickly arranged inspector.
evidence.next_action: Before the close, message the dealer for lifted-carpet and underside photos, the timing-belt and fuel-tank invoices, and tire date codes, and simultaneously ask a mobile inspector in the Dallas area whether they can inspect the car in Wylie tomorrow morning.
